paper.title_en: Interpretation of the LZ Event via Inelastic ALP-Dark Photon Transition with Photon Exchange
paper.abstract_en: The LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment has reported a nuclear recoil event at $248\pm23$~keV with a global significance of about $2.6σ$. We for the first time explain it via the inelastic process with photon mediator. We consider a dark matter (DM) axion-like particle (ALP) $a$ converts into a heavier dark photon $γ'$ via the nuclear electromagnetic current, and study the photon-mediated endothermic transition $aA\rightarrowγ'A$. We derive the kinematics and cross sections for non-relativistic halo and boosted ALPs. A three-bin Poisson fit to the LZ data includes the xenon isotopes, charge form factors, detector efficiency, and energy resolution. Halo DM, which has mass $m\simeq1.2$~TeV, mass splitting $δ\simeq346$~keV, and near the upper coupling bound, reproduces the event with about $61\%$ in the middle bin. Boosted DM with $v_{0}=0.05\,c$ and $Φ_{0}=10^{5}~\mathrm{cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$ requires only $m\simeq5.74$~GeV and $δ\simeq6.66$~MeV to give about $62\%$. We find that a broader Gaussian spread in the incident energy has a significant effect on the fitted masses.
